title: Understanding KDE
text: A Kernel Density Estimate (KDE) is a way to estimate the probability density function of a random variable. It should be smooth and the area under the curve should be $$1$$.

title: Checking the Area Under the Curve
text: To determine if the KDE is valid, check if the area under the curve equals $$1$$. This is a key property of probability density functions.

title: Analyzing the Curve
text: Look at the plot. Does the curve appear to have an area under it that sums to 1?

hintAnswer: No, because the area under the curve is not $$1$$.
title: Properties of a Valid KDE
text: A valid KDE should not have negative values and should integrate to $$1$$ over its domain. Does the curve meet these criteria?
